drafted_from: tool:github:m-bain-whisperx's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs whisperX.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use whisperX on my computer to make captions or subtitles with word-level timings from a video or audio file: the file is talk.mp4." It reads the row, installs whisperX if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: whisperX is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use whisperX on talk.mp4". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:m-bain-whisperx"}.
2. It checks that python, ffmpeg are on your computer, and if whisperX is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX.git ; pip install whisperx.
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input}: whisperx talk.mp4 --compute_type int8 --device cpu --highlight_words True
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: whisperX on a 2 minute talk by Sam, a baker, about her shop
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:m-bain-whisperx runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got whisperX in, the command line: whisperx talk.mp4 --compute_type int8 --device cpu --highlight_words True  (synthetic input: a 2 minute talk by Sam, a baker, about her shop).
worked_examples.hands_back: whisperx loads the model on the CPU in int8, aligns each word to its time and writes the captions beside where it ran: talk.srt, talk.vtt, talk.txt, talk.json and talk.tsv. In talk.srt the first caption reads "1 / 00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,200 / Hi, I am Sam and I run a small bakery." with the word being spoken highlighted because of --highlight_words True.
